A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GIFT, with matching core equations and experiments. The main text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original saliency-localization results, hallucination and general vision-language benchmarks, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and latency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds model and baseline evaluations, layer-selection robustness experiments, token-extraction comparisons, and additional benchmark results.

M1.justification: The default GIFT procedure remains unchanged. Section 5.3 and Appendix F introduce an optional variant that prompts Qwen3-VL 8B to select visually grounded words instead of using POS tagging, changing the token-selection component. Token weighting and bypassing unnecessary saliency computation remain future proposals.

E1.justification: v3 retains the original coverage and adds AMBER's existence, attribute, and relation hallucination tasks and MMBench's perception/reasoning evaluation. Appendix A also introduces MathVista's visual mathematics domain for saliency-layer robustness analysis, extending coverage beyond the original TextVQA analysis.

E2.justification: VCD is added to the LLaVA-1.5 7B and 13B comparisons in Tables 2–3 and to the latency comparison in Table 4. Greedy decoding, VAF, VAR, and Rel-Attn remain; comparisons on Qwen models still use only greedy decoding.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends the evaluation design with Qwen3-VL 8B, controlled enhancement-layer range sweeps, and cross-dataset extraction-layer checks. Added benchmark evaluations reuse the main hyperparameters without retuning and introduce AMBER subscores and MMBench's CircularEval procedure. Existing benchmark splits, decoding budgets, and GPT-4.1 scoring settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining component and enhancement-strength ablations, v3 tests extraction-layer stability across datasets and samples, enhancement-layer range sensitivity, and POS versus LLM word extraction. Appendix H adds saliency case studies for open-ended captioning and weather questions. These address several previously untested robustness and mechanism questions.

E5.justification: Appendix A newly reports five random seeds, each sampling 50 examples, for each of two models on TextVQA and MathVista, with individual-run values in Tables 8–11. Both versions already average five GPT-4.1 scoring repetitions for MMHal-Bench; confidence intervals and significance tests are not added.

E6.justification: Matched original benchmark and component-ablation scores are unchanged, but v3 adds substantial results for VCD, Qwen3-VL, new benchmarks, and robustness studies. Examples include Qwen3-VL MMHal-Bench hallucination rates of 28.3 for greedy decoding versus 26.4 for GIFT, and LLaVA-1.5 7B AMBER scores of 83.9 versus 87.2. Table 7 newly reports 52.6 hallucination rate for LLM extraction versus 57.3 for POS extraction.

T1.justification: The mathematical procedure in Equations 1–7 is retained. Moving min-max normalization from Equations 2–3 into accompanying prose and naming the positive attention increment are equivalent restatements. Neither version introduces theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central hallucination-mitigation, preserved general capability, and low-overhead claims, including the stated 20.7% maximum improvement. The introduction expands the ablation contribution from validating components to also establishing robustness to hyperparameter selection.

C2.justification: v3 interprets extraction-layer stability as evidence of a model-intrinsic property and attributes Qwen3-VL's relatively high CHAIR scores to detailed descriptions interacting with string matching. It also refines v1's broad query-quality limitation into failures involving image-irrelevant content, including retrieved documents, and identifies a missing evaluation scenario for such inputs.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and link, the exact LLM extraction prompt and word-to-token mapping, the COCO localization query template, and Qwen3-VL configuration details. These extend existing documentation; the original hardware, precision choices, scoring model, and decoding budgets remain documented.

R1.justification: Related work adds citations to Sarkar et al., Wu et al., and Qiu et al.; new evaluations add MathVista, AMBER, and MMBench references. The spaCy bibliographic citation becomes a website footnote. GIFT's overall positioning against contrastive decoding, visual-input modification, and attention steering is retained.

P1.justification: v3 tightens prose while retaining the overall narrative and much of the method explanation. The former Analyses section is redistributed into experimental results and Section 5.3 Ablations, appendices are reorganized, and an Impact Statement replaces the separate LLM-use disclosure. Author affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference paper with extensively rearranged displays. Table 3 is transposed, the latency bar chart becomes Table 4, and model plots gain Qwen3-VL panels. New analysis tables and saliency examples are added; the retained qualitative examples are enlarged and redistributed across pages.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses a substantive validation gap through extraction-layer checks across five seeds and two datasets, plus enhancement-layer sensitivity tests. Additional benchmarks evaluated without retuning, VCD and Qwen3-VL comparisons, and code/prompt documentation materially strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. The original overlap between tuning and evaluation samples remains, but the new robustness and transfer evidence substantially improves support for the conclusions.
